newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu tells Israeli opposition he's staying.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu tells Israeli opposition he's staying.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday cautioned in Amman his political opponents against preparing for his early demise over allegations of government corruption.

Netanyahu was visibly embarrassed at a news conference with Jordan's King Hussein when an Israeli reporter asked him about his reaction to an Israeli left-wing lawmaker's call he suspends himself during investigation of allegations of corruption in the appointment of an attorney general last month.
Netanyahu apologised to King Hussein and at first did not respond to the question. But reporters asked he respond.

"I do not intend to relate to the investigation. I will relate to the things I've heard from groups of the opposition. I've heard they are already preparing for new elections, tailoring suits," he said in the live broadcast on Israel Radio.

"I have one suggestion for them: Wait patiently. You have four good years in the opposition. I intend that you will enjoy another four years in the opposition after that...I'm going to continue to lead Israel in my way, to lead to peace, security, and economic prosperity."
The journalist asked Netanyahu if he would confirm he had been warned by police about self-incrimination during questioning.
"I told you I would not relate to the investigation. I did not do it then and I will not relate to it now. I related to the plans of the Labour party, I think you heard my answer," Netanyahu said.
Police questioned Netanyahu for four hours on Tuesday about his short-lived appointment last month of Jerusalem lawyer Roni Bar-On, an activist in his Likud party, as attorney-general.

Israel Television said on January 22 that Shas party leader Aryeh Deri, on trial on corruption charges for the past three years and a key figure in the ruling coalition, had pressed to have Bar-On named to the post to arrange a plea bargain.

According to the television, Deri had demanded Bar-On get the attorney-general job in exchange for Shas' support for Netanyahu's accord with the Palestinian Authority on an Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank town of Hebron last month.
Bar-On quit 12 hours after taking office amid allegations by jurists and politicians that he was not qualified for the job.
Nissim Zvilli, secretary-general of the main opposition Labour party, said it was "beginning preparations for early elections" because the probe could bring down the government.
Labour leader Shimon Peres, who lost last May's election to the Likud party's Netanyahu, declined to say on Sunday whether he would run again for prime minister if a new poll was called.
In remarks to Army Radio, Peres said politicians should first allow police to wrap up their investigation before making a "partisan storm".
Netanyahu, Deri, Bar-On and some 20 others, including cabinet ministers, legislators and lawyers were questioned in the investigation and have denied any wrongdoing.
